Dengue Outbreak Disrupts Panama Electric Utilities, Generadora de Gatun SA Among Affected Firms

PANAMA CITY, June 8—An outbreak of dengue fever has disrupted operations across Panama’s electric utilities sector, with several power generation sites reporting high absenteeism among workers and delays in routine maintenance, industry officials said Saturday.

The Ministry of Health confirmed that more than 60 cases of dengue have been reported among employees at various power plants in the Colón and Panama Oeste provinces over the past two weeks. Generadora de Gatun SA, one of the largest electricity producers in the country, said it has temporarily reduced staffing at its Gatún facility after 18 workers tested positive for the mosquito-borne virus.

“The health and safety of our employees are our top priority,” said Carla Jiménez, spokesperson for Generadora de Gatun SA. “We have increased mosquito control measures and are working closely with authorities to monitor the situation.” She added that while there has been no impact on electricity supply to customers so far, some non-essential maintenance activities have been postponed.

Other companies, including Hidroeléctrica Bahía and Central Térmica Panamá, have also reported staff shortages, according to the National Electric Utilities Association (ANEUP). “Absenteeism rates at some sites have reached 25 percent, which is unprecedented,” said ANEUP president Luis Herrera. “We are urging all companies to reinforce health protocols and coordinate with local health officials.”

Union representatives expressed concern that the outbreak could worsen if mosquito breeding sites around facilities are not eliminated. “Workers are anxious,” said union leader María González. “We need urgent action to prevent further cases.”

Health authorities are conducting fumigation campaigns and distributing information to workers. The outbreak remains ongoing, with officials warning that more cases are expected in the coming days.
